comments.note: In `promptPassword()`, the stty-availability check uses `shell_exec()` which returns null on failure but the condition conflates two things (DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR check and shell_exec result). A more robust check would be `trim(shell_exec('command -v stty 2>/dev/null') ?? '')`. The current logic is safe for the intended use case but could produce a false positive on some restricted Unix environments.

comments.note: In promptPassword() (line 132-133), the stty-availability probe is `shell_exec('stty 2>/dev/null; echo $?')`. Because of the trailing `; echo $?`, this always produces output ('0' or '1') and will never return null — making the null-check ineffective as a real availability guard. In practice on a non-Windows system $sttyAvailable will always be true. The current logic is safe for developer workstations where stty is universally present, but could silently fail on restricted Unix environments (e.g. CI containers with limited proc access). Not blocking for a dev-tools utility; noted for future hardening if the script is ever used in automated pipelines.
